articles.title: GTA 6 not launching, PS5 error, possible reason, solutions, and more
articles.summary: If GTA 6 (Grand Theft Auto VI) refuses to open on your PS5, you're not alone in running into launch-day trouble.
articles.body: If GTA 6 (Grand Theft Auto VI) refuses to open on your PS5, you're not alone in running into launch-day trouble. Most problems come down to a handful of causes, and most can be fixed in minutes.There are a few things that you can check and do to resolve the PS5 errors that you might encounter while you try to open GTA 6. In the section below, we take a detailed look at what to check, solutions, and more.Why GTA 6 might not startListed below are some of the key reasons why GTA 6 might not be starting on your PS5:It isn't unlocked yet. GTA 6 unlocks at midnight local time on November 19, 2026, so a padlock before then is normal.The preload isn't finished. The game needs up to 212 GB, and it won't unlock if it's still downloading.The wrong storage. PS5 games must run from internal storage or a compatible M.2 SSD, and a standard external USB drive may only store the files without letting you play.Outdated software. Sony pushed a last-minute firmware update, version 26.07-14.23.00, ahead of the November 19 launch.Corrupted files or server trouble. A bad install or a PlayStation Network outage can also block the game.Step-by-step fixesConfirm the unlock time and your clock. Check your region's unlock time and make sure your console's date and time are correct. Set them to automatic.Finish the install. Open Downloads/Uploads and make sure GTA 6 shows as complete. Install any game update it asks for.Move it off USB storage. If GTA 6 is on an external USB drive, move it to the PS5's internal storage before launching.Restart and update. Close the game with Options > Close Game, restart the PS5, and install any available game or system updates. The system update is under Settings > System > System Software.Rebuild the database. If problems continue, start in Safe Mode and use Clear Cache and Rebuild Database.Reinstall. For persistent launch failures, PlayStation recommends deleting and re-downloading the game.Common error codesCE-100095-5: The application didn't start correctly. Make sure the game is fully downloaded, past its unlock time, and installed on compatible storage.CE-100028-1: There isn't enough space on your SSD.NW-102636-8: Turn the router off for more than five minutes and restart it, or move the PS5 closer on Wi-Fi.Network and server codes: NW-102216-2, NW-102417-5, and CE-105799-1 point to network trouble. If PSN has issues, the fix is to wait a few minutes and try again.If nothing worksCheck PlayStation's service status first, since a server problem can't be fixed on your end. Then contact PlayStation support and have your error code ready. Jot down any message you see so you don't repeat the same steps.To conclude, you can check the unlock time for your region, finish the install, keep the game on internal storage, update your software, and restore your licenses. Reinstalling is the last resort.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: After 13-year wait, GTA 6 arrives, but even PS5 Pro will never get 60 FPS update as it's 'not powerful enough'
articles.summary: Discover the reasons behind GTA 6's 30 FPS limitation even on the PS5 Pro and the impact of a 13-year wait for the series' latest installment.
articles.body: Thirteen years is a long time to wait for a video game. It is long enough for an entire console generation to come and go, for gaming hardware to change dramatically and for expectations to become almost impossible to satisfy. Yet Grand Theft Auto VI has finally arrived, bringing players back to Vice City and the sprawling state of Leonida. The spectacle is here, but so is an uncomfortable question: why does the biggest game of 2026 run at just 30 frames per second, even on Sony’s most powerful console?GTA 6 arrives, but the 60 FPS expectation has taken a hitRockstar Games launched GTA 6 globally at midnight local time on Thursday, November 19, ending the 13-year wait since Grand Theft Auto V arrived in September 2013. The game is available on PlayStation 5, PS5 Pro and Xbox Series X|S, with an Xbox One option through cloud gaming. Its launch campaign follows Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, while the standalone online multiplayer experience has yet to receive a release date.In India, the Standard Edition is priced at ₹5,999, while the Ultimate Edition costs ₹7,499. Players will also need up to 212GB of free storage, a substantial installation for a game that has spent years being described as one of the most ambitious productions in the medium.One of the more contentious aspects of GTA 6's technical ambitions is its 30 frames-per-second target across supported consoles, with no 60 FPS performance mode available, even on the PS5 Pro. At a time when 60 FPS has become an increasingly familiar option in major releases, the decision feels unusually conservative for a game carrying such enormous expectations.The difference between the two frame rates is particularly noticeable in a game built around constant movement and interaction. At 60 FPS, movement appears smoother, camera turns feel cleaner and controller inputs generally register more immediately. At 30 FPS, that fluidity is reduced, something players are likely to notice during high-speed driving, gunfights and sudden changes in perspective. Console players have also grown accustomed to choosing between visual fidelity and performance, making the absence of that option in GTA 6 all the more significant.The CPU problem behind Rockstar’s 30 FPS decisionThe reason behind the 30 FPS target lies in how Rockstar is approaching the game's technical demands. According to the studio, the main limitation is not the graphics processor but the central processing unit (CPU), which is responsible for handling the calculations that keep the world running, from character behaviour and traffic systems to the wider activity unfolding across the mapRendering GTA 6's visual effects is only part of the technical challenge. The CPU must also keep track of everything happening within the world, including pedestrian behaviour, traffic, physics, artificial intelligence and the interactions between them. With Rockstar aiming to create an environment that feels densely populated and constantly responsive, the amount of information the processor has to handle at any given moment can become substantialThe difference becomes clearer when looking at the time available to process each frame. At 30 FPS, the console has 33.3 milliseconds to complete the necessary calculations and render a frame. Doubling the frame rate to 60 FPS cuts that window to just 16.7 milliseconds. For Rockstar, that means asking the hardware to handle the same complex world simulation in half the time, potentially requiring compromises to the systems that make the game feel alive.Technology production director Marc Chambers addressed the issue in an interview with Kotaku, explaining why even the PS5 Pro cannot overcome the limitation.“While the PS5 Pro's central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game's complex simulation at higher frame rates.”That is an important distinction for anyone wondering why switching off a few graphical effects cannot magically produce 60 FPS. Reducing resolution or ray tracing can ease the GPU's workload, but it does not necessarily solve a CPU bottleneck. The problem, as Rockstar describes it, lies in processing the world itself.Why the PS5 Pro cannot rescue the frame rateExpectations are arguably higher for the PS5 Pro, given that Sony positioned it as a more powerful version of its console, with improved hardware designed to deliver better performance and visual quality. Owners who invested in the upgraded model could reasonably expect to see those gains reflected in a release as significant as GTA 6, making the absence of a 60 FPS option particularly disappointing.The PS5 Pro does bring visual improvements, although they do not extend to frame rate. Chambers explained that the standard version already features ray-traced reflections and global illumination, while the Pro adds ray-traced shadows and uses PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) to improve image clarity. Rather than targeting smoother performance, the additional GPU power and upscaling technology are being used to enhance the visual detail of Leonida.Rockstar co-studio head and head of development Rob Nelson was even more direct when IGN asked about the compromises required to achieve 60 FPS.Chambers was clear that pushing for a higher frame rate would have required too many sacrifices to the overall experience. “Too much, too much,” he said. “It wouldn’t have been acceptable to anybody. The simple answer is, when you ask the technical team, they're, like, 'Have you seen it?' There’s too many compromises that would've had to have been made to do that, is the short answer.”Rockstar's reasoning is understandable, given that a performance mode would require more than simply increasing the frame rate. However, it leaves PS5 Pro owners with improved visuals but the same 30 FPS ceiling as players on the standard console. More significantly, Chambers told Kotaku that Rockstar does not expect to introduce either a 40 FPS or 60 FPS mode on current-generation consoles.Thirty frames per second is one thing; keeping it stable is anotherThe 30 FPS target also makes consistency particularly important, since even minor drops can make an already less fluid experience feel worse. Digital Foundry's technical analysis found that the PS5 Pro handled this well, with John Linneman describing its performance as a “near-flawless 30fps”. The standard PS5 was less consistent, with more frequent dips during regular gameplay and greater strain during demanding sequences involving extensive destruction.The consistency of that performance is just as important as the frame rate itself. How evenly frames are delivered, known as frame pacing, has a direct effect on how smooth a game feels. A stable 30 FPS can provide a reasonably coherent experience, but when performance drops below that level, movement can become uneven and controls may feel less responsive.Rockstar's approach prioritises the complexity of the game world over a higher frame rate, keeping its traffic systems, crowds, lighting and environmental detail intact rather than scaling them back to accommodate 60 FPS. The studio's position is that making those compromises would come at the expense of the experience it wants players to have.A choice players have not been givenThere is a legitimate argument for prioritising the complexity of an open world over a higher frame rate. Rockstar has built its reputation on environments that feel alive, and GTA 6 is clearly intended to take that approach further. But players are equally justified in asking why they cannot decide for themselves whether they would prefer that visual fidelity or a smoother, more responsive game.The absence of a day-one PC version makes the decision more frustrating for enthusiasts who would ordinarily look to more powerful hardware for higher frame rates. Rockstar has not announced a PC release window, leaving console players with no immediate alternative.After 13 years, GTA 6 has arrived with the scale, ambition and scrutiny that accompany a release of this magnitude. The 30 FPS decision does not automatically make it a lesser game, but neither should Rockstar's technical ambitions exempt it from criticism. A world can be extraordinary to look at and still leave players wishing it responded more quickly. For now, the studio has decided which side of that compromise matters more.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: GTA 6 graphics settings on Xbox: How to get the best visual experience
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI runs on both Xbox Series X and Series S, but the picture you get depends on how your console and display are set up.
articles.body: Grand Theft Auto VI runs on both Xbox Series X and Series S, but the picture you get depends on how your console and display are set up. The game itself has limited options, so you need to make the most out of them.If you want to optimize your overall experiece, tweaking the settings will help you out immensely. In the section below, we take a look at how you can get the best visual experience on Xbox.GTA 6 Xbox settings guideListed below are the settings that you can apply for the optimal experience on GTA 6:SettingXbox Series XXbox Series SResolution4K UHD (based on your display)t1080pHDROnOnVRROnOnTV Motion SmoothingOffOffHGiGOnOnAudioToggle on 360 Spatial SoundToggle on 360 Spatial SoundResolutionGTA 6 supports 4K on the Series X, which makes it the better way to play on that console. If you have a 4K display, set your Xbox output to 4K UHD. On the Series S, stick with 1080p. The smaller console is unlikely to handle 4K well, and a lower resolution should give you a better experience.HDRHDR is supported, so turn on HDR10 on both consoles if your TV or monitor can handle it. If your display doesn't support HDR, leave it off, since a mismatch can wash out colors. Where available, enable HGiG as well. It helps your console and display coordinate brightness so highlights aren't clipped.Refresh rate and VRRGTA 6 is locked at 30 FPS on both Series X and Series S. A display with a higher refresh rate won't change that, but Variable Refresh Rate still helps. With VRR turned on, your screen adjusts its refresh rate to match the game's frame rate, which reduces tearing and judder. If VRR isn't available, you can instead lock your refresh rate to 30 Hz, which can make motion feel smoother.TV settingsTurn off TV Motion Smoothing. This feature adds artificial frames, which can introduce input lag and give the game an unnatural, soap-opera look. Most TVs have a Game Mode that disables this processing automatically, so that's worth using too.AudioThe game's soundtrack is a big part of its atmosphere, so audio matters. If your setup supports it, enable 360 Spatial Sound, and use headphones for the best effect. It makes Vice City's radio and street ambience feel more immersive.Quick checklistSet your output resolution to 4K (Series X) or 1080p (Series S).Turn on HDR10 and HGiG if your display supports them.Enable VRR.Switch off TV Motion Smoothing, or use Game Mode.Turn on 360 Spatial Sound.The best Xbox setup for GTA 6 comes down to matching your resolution to your console, turning on HDR10 and VRR, and disabling motion smoothing. With the game fixed at 30 FPS, display settings do most of the work in getting a clean, stable image.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

The suggested location is Kingfishers camp, near the water south of Hamlet. However, timing and character choice seem to matter.Players reportedly need to explore the area at night while controlling Jason. Those who encounter Skunkape should not expect an easy chase. The creature quickly disappears, leaving players with more questions than answers.The discovery has also caught the attention of the GTA community, with gameplay clips and sightings beginning to circulate across streaming platforms and social media.How to unlock the GTA 6 Skunkape questFinding Skunkape is only the beginning. This interaction reportedly unlocks the next stage of the mystery, with a marker appearing on the map to guide players towards further investigations.For now, the full quest remains something of an unknown. Since GTA 6 has only just launched, players are still working through its hidden events and discovering what Rockstar has tucked away across the map.The mystery also raises an interesting question: is Skunkape simply another unusual creature encounter, or does Rockstar have a much bigger surprise waiting at the end of the quest?Players looking to investigate should first complete the opening mission, switch to Jason, and visit Kingfishers camp after dark. articles.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 turns 24 hours into a historic moment with 3 record-breaking achievements
articles.summary: GTA 6 was still locked in North America when the first records fell.
articles.body: GTA 6 was still locked in North America when the first records fell. Players in New Zealand got it first, and streamers in the United States used Xbox workarounds to start early. By 12:30 UTC on launch day, live viewership across Twitch, YouTube and Kick had passed 6.38 million at once, close to four times the old mark from the Valorant closed beta. Later counts put the combined peak near 8 million.The effect spread past streaming. On Wednesday evening, internet exchange operator DE-CIX recorded its highest data throughput ever, and Twitch handed GTA 6 a title League of Legends had held since 2022. The game is on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S, and the load showed fast.How big were GTA 6’s launch-day streaming records?The peak splits across three platforms. Twitch reached 3.31 million concurrent viewers, YouTube 3.22 million and Kick 1.5 million. The Twitch figure matters most, because it ends League of Legends’ run as the category with the highest peak viewership on the site. That mark came from the 2022 World Championship final between T1 and DRX.Twitch’s own data fills in the rest. Viewership on the platform is up 111% from the same point last week, and the site counted “tens of millions of hours watched” after only “just a couple hours in.” Put another way, the total equals more than 1,500 years of nonstop viewing.Individual streamers moved the needle too. Rubius had 311,000 people watching within an hour of going live. The old Twitch record for a single game stood at 1.7 million concurrent viewers, set by Valorant in 2020. GTA 6 has smashed it.Early access, a Metacritic 99 and what comes nextThe Xbox loopholes explain why numbers jumped before the US launch. Streamers started in the early morning hours, and viewers followed.The internet traffic story reaches well beyond gaming. DE-CIX said throughput across its exchanges worldwide hit 33.03 terabits per second at 20:20 Central European Time on 18 November. The company puts that at 25% above where traffic stood at the start of the year.Reviews help explain the pull. GTA 6 holds a Metacritic average of 99, the highest in the site’s history.How long the numbers last is open. Some streamers think the game pays off for a couple of weeks. Others believe it can be mined for months and years. Twitch says GTA 5 has collected 9 billion hours watched over its lifetime, and a PC release is rumored for early next year, with the online mode expected in 2027.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: GTA 6 Easter egg hunt gets darker as players uncover Dexter Morgan’s apartment and more TV references
articles.summary: Players have found a copy of Dexter Morgan’s Miami apartment building in GTA 6.
articles.body: Players have found a copy of Dexter Morgan’s Miami apartment building in GTA 6. Rockstar named it Trinity Apartments, a nod to the Trinity Killer, the villain John Lithgow played in the fourth season of the show. Footage shows the complex looks almost identical to the one Morgan lived in during the original series, which ran from 2006 to 2013. Players can drive up to it, climb to the roof and find tools fans will know well. A boat modeled on his is docked nearby. Rockstar has packed the game with detail, and this is likely one of many TV references.Where is Dexter Morgan’s apartment in GTA 6 and what can players do there?Trinity Apartments is in the game’s version of Miami, and players can reach it by car. The building is open to walk around, though the apartment itself is not. Head up to the roof and you will find a knife, plastic wrap, duct tape and a syringe. Fans of the series will know what each item was for, since Morgan relied on all of them when he went after his victims.Look at the outside wall and you will also spot the AC unit where he kept his blood slide trophies in the show. Rockstar did not skip the small stuff.The water has its own nod. Down at the docks, players can take a boat that looks like the Slice of Life, the one Morgan used to carry bodies out to sea. Once aboard, they can explore the surrounding waters.Dexter: Resurrection is airing its second season, and like New Blood before it, the show is set in New York. Even so, Morgan is still tied to Miami and Florida culture, which makes the GTA 6 version feel like a natural fit.GTA 6 launch hype brings economic estimates and new criticismInterest in the game is huge. Reviewers have called it a masterpiece and said it was worth the 13-year wait. Pre-sale records have fallen, and revenue has already passed $1 billion. Projections put lifetime revenue at an extra $10 billion.The money is not the only number getting attention. Economists estimate 1.5 million people could miss work to play, which could cost the U.S. about $1 billion in lost productivity.Not everyone is cheering. Kayleigh McEnany took up the debate over games and violence on a Thursday broadcast, and she pointed to people watching others play online. “These places can be a breeding ground for this kind of violence,” she said. Her comments came during a wider discussion about whether games can be blamed for real-world violence and what part they play in it.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Marine Corps hero under federal investigation
articles.summary: Retired Sgt. Maj. Bradley Kasal, whose bloodied visage was depicted in an iconic Iraq War photo, is under investigation stemming from his tenure as a high sc...
articles.body:
Henderson, Nevada — One of the most celebrated Marine Corps veterans, whose heroism during the Iraq War earned him the nation's second-highest award for combat valor and a place in military history, is the subject of a criminal investigation over allegations stemming from his tenure as a high school instructor for a Junior Reserve Officers' Training Corps, CBS News has learned.

Retired Sgt. Maj. Bradley Kasal, who served in the Marine Corps for 34 years, is under investigation by the Naval Criminal Investigative Service, the primary federal law enforcement agency for matters involving the Navy and Marine Corps.

The allegations against the highly decorated Marine veteran have not been disclosed by the law enforcement agency. However, federal agencies told CBS News that the investigation concerns the period of time when he worked as a JROTC instructor at the Basic Academy of International Studies. The academy is a public high school in Henderson, Nevada, operated by the Clark County School District.

The federal investigation marks a dramatic turn for a Marine whose actions on the battlefield made him a symbol of military courage. Kasal's heroism was captured in a 2004 photograph showing him in the Second Battle of Fallujah. His uniform was soaked in blood, and he was being helped out of a building by two Marines. His right leg was shattered, and his body riddled with gunshot wounds and grenade fragments, but he still gripped a pistol and combat knife. The scene was later immortalized in statues installed at two Marine bases. He retired after 34 years of service and was the recipient of two Purple Hearts and the Navy Cross, the second-highest decoration for combat valor, behind the Medal of Honor.

On Wednesday, the Marine Corps told CBS News that the service is "aware of the allegations against a retired Marine Sergeant Major which occurred while he was employed as a civilian JROTC instructor by the Basic Academy of International Studies."

The Marine Corps also said that the Naval Criminal Investigative Service "is actively investigating the allegations, as the Department of the Navy's lead for felony-level criminal investigations."

Separately, Denise Caskey of NCIS confirmed that its field office at Camp Pendleton in California is conducting the investigation.

NCIS does not typically confirm active investigations, making this an unusual case. The agency commonly investigates matters of homicide, sexual assault, fraud and even terrorism and espionage cases. The agency also conducts counterintelligence investigations, working with other federal agencies to identify threats to national security.

Kasal did not reply to CBS News' multiple attempts to contact him.

CBS News traveled to Henderson, Nevada, and over the course of the last two weeks spoke to nearly 40 people, including former students, school district employees, city officials, parents, U.S. military service members and Marine veterans who served with Kasal. Some asked for anonymity because they were not authorized to speak publicly or feared reprisal.

The cadets CBS News spoke to alleged Kasal often gave rides home to a select group of female cadets. He would take them to Starbucks and spend time with certain students outside of school-sponsored functions. Some also described instances when he was alone with a cadet in a room.

A former school district employee told CBS News that Kasal was advised on several occasions about the perceptions surrounding his relationships with students and was warned against putting himself in potentially compromising situations, including being alone in a room with a cadet.

One former female cadet described developing an unusually close relationship with Kasal after meeting him in 2020, when she was 14. She said she confided in him about difficulties at home and personal matters, including her relationships with boys. After knowing her for barely a year, Kasal offered to adopt her, saying in a text message, "I'm not asking as charity. I'm asking because your [sic] wanted."

When her family members learned of Kasal's offer, she said, they made it clear that adoption was not an option. She said that her relationship with Kasal continued, and she remained comfortable confiding in him about deeply personal matters. The cadet alleged some of their conversations involved sexual rumors that had been spread about her and why Kasal believed some of the problems she was experiencing stemmed from her relationship with her father. In retrospect, she said she realizes that those conversations were inappropriate for an instructor to have with a teenage student.

She now says she thinks Kasal crossed other boundaries, alleging that Kasal invited certain cadets to spend time at his home and at his cabin, she said, including for at least one birthday celebration. He did not extend invitations to everyone in the program. She also claimed that Kasal drove one student home nearly every day.

The Clark County School District told CBS News Kasal was hired by the school district three months after he retired from the Marine Corps, in August 2018. He resigned in August 2025, the school district said.

Enrollment in Basic Academy's JROTC program fluctuates from year to year, averaging roughly 135 students. The program is overseen by a senior Marine instructor and a senior enlisted leader.

When Kasal transitioned from the Marine Corps to the high school JROTC program, he sought to restructure it to more closely resemble the military service.

Some former cadets described him as professional and organized, crediting him with establishing strict standards and bringing a sense of discipline to the program. They also praised the time, energy and personal resources he devoted to his students.

Samantha Francisco, 22, who was in the program from 2018 to 2022, said, "I can't say enough about how amazing he was," and that "he genuinely cared about everybody and taught us incredible lessons." She added that she and her husband, who was also in the JROTC program, still talk weekly about Kasal or something he taught them.

Ashley Vazquez Romo, 22, another cadet from that period, said Kasal "poured his heart and soul into the program." She recalled that he sometimes helped pay for program outings and purchased equipment, including a CPR training mannequin, so students could practice.

Damien Greenwell, 22, who participated in the JROTC program from 2018 to 2022, told CBS News that he deeply respects Kasal for his military service and mentorship, especially to cadets with a troubled home life. But Greenwell also said that over the years he questioned Kasal's conduct on several occasions, adding that even if the decorated Marine's intentions were innocent, his actions could appear inappropriate to an outside observer.

"He would mentor us on how to be a proper leader — which is his job — but he would go a bit beyond this. Sergeant Major [Kasal] helps people in a time of need and that's very honorable," Greenwell said.

"If someone couldn't eat, he would pay for their food. If someone didn't have a ride home, he would help them out. It's awesome, it's great and very commendable," Greenwell said. "But if you're regularly getting Starbucks for a girl … it looks kind of weird … and with driving people home on a consistent basis, it looks bad. You need to have a certain kind of boundary between you and students."

Greenwell told CBS News he remembers a night that still "shocks him a little." It happened in 2024, two years after Greenwell graduated.

Greenwell claimed he went to Lowe's home improvement store around 9 p.m. and saw Kasal's truck in the parking lot. In the store, he observed Kasal walking with a student who he believes was a senior at the high school or a newly minted graduate.

"It was just really weird to me," Greenwell said, recalling that he briefly exchanged greetings with Kasal and the student before the two continued down the aisle. CBS News is withholding the student's name for privacy reasons.

Greenwell said over the years of observing Kasal, he developed doubts about him. He believed the optics could be interpreted as inappropriate, but at the same time wonders if Kasal could just be trying to help students navigate the difficulties of life. But even if he found a relationship between Kasal and a student odd, he was "not gonna say anything. Like, who am I to tell [a] sergeant major?"

Daniel Gillian, who participated in the program from 2018 to 2022 and later enlisted in the Marine Corps, said JROTC was good for him and that Kasal was part of the reason he ended up joining.

The program "gave me a lot of structure and discipline," Gillian said, adding that Kasal helped him "become a better person overall, and once you become a better person, things will fall into place for you."

Gillian said he never witnessed Kasal engage in inappropriate behavior. He sees Kasal as having made an effort to create memorable experiences for students by organizing group hikes, camping trips and other activities outside the classroom. He said Kasal recognized that some students did not have a good home life, and he wanted to make the JROTC program enjoyable and inclusive, emphasizing that all cadets were invited to participate.

Still, he acknowledged that Kasal appeared to favor certain cadets, sometimes buying them coffee, for instance. Gillian said Kasal had also bought coffee for him, but he didn't think it was inappropriate, describing him as a "nice guy."

Gillian also alleged Kasal would take cadets on hikes without seeking permission from the school, but he said this was more a matter of convenience. The hiking trail was only a few minutes away from Basic Academy.

"It was about a 10-minute drive from Basic, and [about] 20 cadets would go. Whoever wanted to go, they would go. We would all carpool," Gillian said, and the hikes were just about an hour.

"Legally, you gotta get [trips] ran through the school, and they gotta approve of it, … but [Kasal is] not gonna wait for [the school] to take two weeks to [approve] an event that takes one day to get back."

One former male cadet, who joined the program in 2019 and now serves in the U.S. military, alleged that Kasal invited him to visit his cabin in Iowa over the summer.

The trip was not school-sponsored, he said, and "it was just going to be the two of us." He says he declined the invitation because he was playing a sport that summer. At the time, he said, he did not consider the invitation to be inappropriate, believing Kasal had extended it because they shared an interest in the sport.

Greenwell said that at one point, he heard a rumor that Kasal was trying to adopt a fellow cadet but that he didn't believe it was true. When CBS News told him that Kasal had offered to adopt a former female cadet, Greenwell said he was "very surprised, shocked and disappointed."

"Even if you have the best intentions in the world, it still looks bad, no matter how you put it, because she's a minor," said Greenwell.

The Defense Department and local school districts share responsibility for overseeing JROTC programs because they are federally sponsored and operate in high schools nationwide. Although instructors are employed by school districts, they must also be certified by their respective military branches, which are responsible for monitoring their professional conduct and ensuring compliance with military standards.

The military services certify and oversee instructors, while school districts handle employment decisions, classroom supervision and compliance with local education policies.

JROTC instructors must acknowledge in writing that they will not engage in prohibited activities between JROTC instructors and students. The rules ban instructors from developing personal, intimate or sexual relationships with cadets, engaging in inappropriate communications and attending social gatherings with students on a personal basis. The restrictions apply from an instructor's first contact with a cadet until six months after the student leaves the JROTC program.

Under the rules, instructors are generally not allowed to give students rides in their personal vehicles, including rides home from school. Exceptions may be made when a student's safety or welfare is at risk or for official school functions involving multiple students. The rules specifically prohibit an instructor from transporting a single student in their personal vehicles.

Instructors are also not allowed to have cadets or other students in their homes. Other interactions, such as purchasing coffee or refreshments for students, are not explicitly prohibited. But such interactions could raise questions about compliance with the rules.

Instructors must sign the acknowledgment before beginning their duties as JROTC instructors and recertify it annually.

When CBS News received the initial news tip regarding Kasal, the Marine Corps said it was aware of allegations and of an investigation, but made no mention of NCIS' involvement.

The Henderson Police Department initially said it had no record of a complaint about Kasal. The Clark County Detention Center and the Clark County District Attorney's Office also did not have any complaints about Kasal on file when contacted some two weeks ago.

Later, during that same period, a spokesperson for the Henderson Police Department said the Clark County School District Police Department was handling the matter. Multiple calls and emails to the Clark County School District and the school district's police department went unanswered. Lt. Bryan Zink of the Clark County School District police department referred inquiries to the school district.

Last week, when CBS News emailed to check in on its inquiry, an email sent in error to CBS News asked a human resources manager to "disregard the request."

When CBS News asked why the request for information was being disregarded, Bryan Callahan, the district's public information officer, emailed for the first time: "We are looking into your request."

When questioned by a CBS News reporter in Henderson earlier this week, Callahan said he was not aware of an investigation of Kasal by the Clark County School District or the school district's police department.

Before he retired from active duty, Kasal reflected on his time in Iraq. The Second Battle of Fallujah in November 2004 was the bloodiest battle involving U.S. Marines since the Vietnam War, marked by brutal house-to-house fighting against Iraqi insurgents.

In 2018, Kasal told CBS News' David Martin that he had entered the building to rescue fellow Marines trapped by insurgent gunfire during one of the war's bloodiest battles. By the time he emerged, Kasal had been shot seven times, shielded a wounded Marine from an exploding grenade and refused medical treatment until others received care.

His actions earned him his second Purple Heart and the Navy Cross.

The photograph of Kasal became an iconic symbol of Marine resilience and sacrifice. The Marine Corps Heritage Foundation named a photojournalism award for Kasal.

The photograph inspired a bronze statue called the "No Man Left Behind" monument, which is installed at both Camp Pendleton in California and Camp Lejeune in North Carolina, according to the Marine Times. The sculpture was the work of John Phelps, a Navy Vietnam veteran whose son Chance was killed in Iraq in 2004, the newspaper reported.

When CBS News first learned about the criminal investigation into Kasal earlier this month, the retired sergeant major was in New York as the guest of honor at an event hosted by the NYPD Marine Corps Association to commemorate 251 years since the founding of the U.S. Marine Corps and honor Marines who also serve as New York City police officers. The New York Post reported that Kasal was presented a framed retirement shadowbox by NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch at police headquarters in Manhattan.

James LaPorta reported from Henderson, Nevada. Julia Kimani Burnham and Eleanor Watson reported from Washington, D.C.

Editor's note: For the past three years, James LaPorta has served as a judge for the Marine Corps Heritage Foundation annual awards program. He has never judged the award category named for retired Sgt. Maj. Bradley Kasal.

articles.title: Cricket's billion-dollar blind spot: The search for a global gaming franchise
articles.summary: As Grand Theft Auto VI finally arrives, 13 years after its predecessor, the excitement surrounding one of gaming's biggest franchises is a reminder of
articles.body: As Grand Theft Auto VI finally arrives, 13 years after its predecessor, the excitement surrounding one of gaming's biggest franchises is a reminder of what a truly enduring video game can mean to its audience. The anticipation has been years in the making, with GTA V continuing to command a massive following even as an entire generation of gaming technology has evolved around it.Cricket gaming has its own version of that nostalgia, although without quite the same succession of blockbusters. Nearly two decades after its release, EA Sports Cricket 07 continues to find a place in conversations among fans, many of whom still regard it as a benchmark for the genre. There have been attempts to fill that void, from the Don Bradman series to Ashes Cricket and more recent mobile titles, some of which have reached millions of downloads, but cricket is yet to produce a game that can build the kind of sustained global following enjoyed by EA Sports FC or NBA 2K.The International Cricket Council, too, is now looking at that space more seriously. What began with a global call for expressions of interest in 2025 to develop a flagship mobile cricket game moved into a formal tender process in April this year, with some of the biggest names in gaming, including Electronic Arts, Big Ant Studios and Krafton, alongside Indian companies such as Reliance Jio, Nazara Technologies and Dream Cricket, reported to be among those interested. The rights framework being considered by the ICC covers player names, images and likenesses, tournament data and branding across mobile and console platforms, although the process has involved several stages of evaluation and the final arrangement has not been publicly confirmed.It is a fairly crowded field for a category that has struggled to produce a lasting global franchise. Cricket has had its share of successful titles and loyal players, but the interest has not quite translated into a game that travels beyond the sport's traditional markets, or one that can keep players engaged over several years. The ICC's move has brought the commercial side of that opportunity into focus, but for developers the question is a little more basic: what has been missing from cricket games all these years, and what would it take to get it right?The cricket gaming industry's missing global franchiseKaran Shroff, co-founder of Bengaluru-based LightFury Games, believes there is still a sizeable gap to be filled. The company is developing eCricket, a mobile-first title that it hopes will go beyond the familiar format of a cricket game and build into a longer-term gaming property. But Shroff's ambition is not restricted to making another cricket game. He wants to build a gaming studio from India that can create intellectual property for a global audience, with eCricket serving as its first major test."While eCricket is our first product and it's the first game that we'll build as a startup, all our energy and focus is on that. But we are not a one-game, one-product company. So LightFury is a AAA studio and a game tech company and that's the vision that we're building on," Shroff tells Timesofindia.com."Imagine if, I mean you look at China, they have Tencent, they have NetEase, you look at the US, they have EA, they have Rockstar, you look at France, they have Ubisoft and so on and so forth. But what does India have from a gaming company? Not too much, unfortunately. And that's something that we want to change worldwide. We want to build AAA IPs from India that go global."Building more than just another cricket gameThe choice of cricket came from looking at a category where there was already an audience, but where he felt the larger opportunity had not been explored."When we got together we were like, okay, what space has a white space broadly where there hasn't been a AAA product but there is a market to capture. And cricket was of course there. There were a lot of mid-core, casual games that are doing well, but not a AAA title," he said."When you look at that market, they have 100, 200 million downloads but poor retention. And that's something we wanted to bridge. High-quality products, you know, AAA products are built with all the bells and whistles, be it the progression, the task system, the meta system, the monetisation and how you go about the journey within a game, the storytelling, the fidelity, all of those things matter a lot when you build a AAA title. And it's a long journey, it takes years to get there."The history of cricket games is not short. Titles such as Graham Gooch's Test Cricket, Brian Lara Cricket and the EA Sports Cricket series appeared across successive generations of consoles and computers. Cricket 07, released in November 2006, became the last EA Sports cricket game for home consoles and PC. Codemasters' Brian Lara series also had a following, with its 2005 release reaching the top of the UK all-formats sales chart.The genre did not stop there. Big Ant Studios developed the Don Bradman Cricket series before moving to Ashes Cricket and the Cricket titles that followed. Its latest release, Cricket 26, includes an expanded Ashes mode, a management career mode and a Pro Team format with multiplayer competition. Mobile developers have also built their own audiences through titles such as Real Cricket.The continued presence of these games points to an audience, but the challenge has been keeping players engaged and finding a following beyond cricket's established markets. Shroff believes two areas in particular have held cricket games back: licensing and the way the sport is recreated in the game."One is of course the licensing. So, you know, we misspell the names. We don't have accurate licences for things. I think that's a very important aspect of what we do. So we've gone ahead and closed about 600 cricketers overall, and everybody from Rohit to Dhoni to Jos Buttler to Joe Root, we have all of these guys and many more," he said."Every player in our game is a real-world athlete. So no fake names, you know, and they look like themselves, they play like themselves."LightFury has secured licences for more than 600 cricketers through its partnership with Winners Alliance, with players from several major cricketing nations included in the roster. For Shroff, licensing is not simply about getting the names and faces of popular cricketers into the game. It is also about making sure their abilities are reflected in how they play."You can't build a AAA title and not have the right athlete. It shows the seriousness behind the vision and the thought process, which is very clear from day one, that every athlete in the game will be a real-world athlete. Not just from a look and likeness perspective but even from the way they play in game," he said."So, for example, can you bowl and bat with an MSD? No. And can you wicket-keep with a Hardik Pandya? No. You can place him as a wicketkeeper but he'll be an awful wicketkeeper. On the other hand, you bowl with an MSD, he won't be a good bowler. That needs to apply overall from a gameplay perspective as well. You take Hardik Pandya, one of the best all-rounders in the world, you should have that experience and leverage in gameplay."The licensing and gameplay challengeThe licensing effort also feeds into the game's Ultimate Squad format, where players can build a team by bringing together cricketers from different countries and eras. Rather than being restricted to an existing international or domestic side, users can assemble a squad around the players they want, with individual attributes intended to influence how they perform in the game."The way we are building our team is on the back of the Ultimate Squad. So you will have your progression where you complete tasks and move forward. But you will also have the opportunity, as you complete tasks, to get rewards and then go and unlock better cards and build your Ultimate Squad and then take that online and compete with other players. If you beat them again, you get better rewards and you're able to build a better team," Shroff said."So you're kind of chasing your ultimate squad broadly. Like can I have hypothetically Rohit, Dhoni, Bumrah, Pandya, Jos Buttler, Joe Root, all of these guys in one team? And Bumrah opening the bowling attack, can I have it? I can, but I need to play and make that progression and build my ultimate squad."LightFury plans to launch with multiplayer and Ultimate Squad, while a career mode and other features are expected to be introduced later. Shroff said the company has mapped out more than three years of development and content, with new features to be added as players become familiar with the game."All of the other features that you're talking about, in terms of can I start my journey in cricket and go all the way through, when a match is being played can I have a play-along moment, all of that is something that we'll build in the future. But as of now when we go live, it's a AAA title so we won't have all the features when we ship. It's a live-services game, we'll keep adding it incrementally," he said.Building an ecosystem around the gameThere is also a commercial calculation behind that approach as LightFury intends to follow a freemium model, with in-app purchases as its primary source of revenue. Players will be able to buy in-game currency, player packs and other items, while those who do not want to spend money can earn currency through reward-based advertising. The company says it does not intend to interrupt matches with advertisements, with ads restricted to reward-based options in the near future."I think it's always IAPs (In-App Purchases), as a business, as a game. And if you look at any of the success worldwide, they are a very thriving economy within the game. And they're driven by IAPs. They're not driven by ads. And that's what we want to do as well. We want to thrive on IAPs," Shroff said."Of course we will have ads. So it's a freemium kind of a model. So you can either buy currency in game or you can buy a player pack, which is randomized and you end up landing a player and you go about building your ultimate squad. Or you could watch several ads and collect some currency and still go ahead and buy that."He said the company was conscious of the experience during matches. "One thing that we are very conscious of is user experience. So you will not see ads in game when you're playing, at least for the near future. We're never going to do that. But you will see ads only reward-based."The scale of the Indian gaming market gives developers a substantial audience to work with, although the numbers need to be read in the context of how different reports define a gamer. The FICCI-EY Media and Entertainment Report 2026 estimated that India's gamer base reached between 515 million and 525 million in 2025, with more than 100 million people playing games daily.A separate Dentsu-IWMBuzz India Gaming Report 2026 estimated 535 million past-year pure-play gamers, including 332 million who had played in the previous three months and 109 million current paying gamers. It valued the pure-play gaming market at Rs 14,344 crore in 2026. The two sets of figures use different definitions and measurement periods, but underline the scale of the audience that India's gaming industry can potentially reach.India's gaming opportunity and the global ambitionThe bigger challenge is turning that audience into successful home-grown intellectual property that can compete internationally. Shroff wants eCricket to find players in countries where cricket does not have the cultural presence it enjoys in India, England or Australia. He believes gaming can introduce people to the sport before they begin following it."100%. 100%. I'll tell you why. The next generation of audience isn't going to be passive. They're not going to just sit and watch. They're going to be immersed in the sport. They're going to want to be a part of it in some fashion and manner," he said."Our generation, we all had a say on what the team should be, who should open, why is he bowling, and they shouldn't have got him now, they should have given it to this bowler. This was our social layer on the game which we would have conversations around. We're all passionate about the sport. Similarly, the coming generation is more immersed in the sport. They want to actually be involved in that."He pointed to the way audiences now engage with sports through content and gaming, rather than only watching matches."It's also easy to pick and play. Downloading a game is easy and you learn the ropes while you play the game. It's fun and engaging versus actually taking the sport and going there. The game reaches faster than the sport in a lot of geographies and then eventually the sport reaches there if the game has good penetration," he said.He drew comparisons with football, WWE and poker, where gaming has helped people become familiar with sports or formats they may not otherwise have followed. For cricket, the possibility is relevant in markets such as the United States, Germany and Japan, where the sport has a smaller following than in India, England or Australia.The competition for players' time and spending is considerable. Electronic Arts reported net revenue of $7.53 billion for the financial year ended March 2026, with its global football franchise among the major contributors. Its filings also underline the importance of live services and additional in-game content to the business. Building a successful sports game is not just about selling a title; it is about maintaining a player base and a commercial relationship over several years.Cricketers back LightFury's global ambitionsLightFury has also brought several prominent cricketers into the company as investors. MS Dhoni, Jasprit Bumrah, Hardik Pandya, Shreyas Iyer, Ravindra Jadeja, Tilak Varma and Sai Sudharsan have backed the studio, with Rohit Sharma subsequently joining the group. Their involvement brings visibility and a direct connection with the sport, but Shroff was careful not to suggest that the cricketers are involved in the day-to-day development of the title."They don't have too much time to give us. Like most investors, the founders have to do the building. Investors come in with support when you need it. But we have to do all the heavyweight lifting," he said.He added that some players have asked to receive new builds of the game so they can play them and offer feedback. LightFury also works with Ranji and former IPL cricketers on aspects of the product, while the company looks to use the experience of current players to understand what feels right and what needs to change.The studio has said it has received more than 300,000 early-access sign-ups. Shroff said the response on social media and YouTube has been encouraging, with gamers also getting an opportunity to play-test the title ahead of its wider release. But he was clear that early registrations and attention are not the ultimate measure of success for the company."The vision from day one is to build the best cricket game in the world and be a global franchise built from India for the world. I can give you numbers saying this is what it would mean, this is what profitability would mean. But I think for us, the biggest win is when the gamers, when India loves the game to begin with, because that's where we're going live first. And then gamers across the world love the cricket game," he said."Everybody has said cricket has missed what it should have had. So the day they say, now eCricket is that game, it's a win for us because everything else is a subset. Everything else follows. Once you have the consumer's love and you have their validation, I think that's the validation I would always be hungry for."Can eCricket become India's first global cricket gaming franchise?For Shroff, the opportunity is bigger than one title. He sees a cricket gaming property creating work for developers, gaming influencers, creators and people involved in tournaments and sponsorships, with the game eventually becoming the centre of a wider digital cricket ecosystem."If you ask me where we would be in 2030, we would have created thousands of jobs, we would have created an ecosystem on the back of this, that would be digitally, I mean cricket digitally would transform on the back of this and also it would be the first billion-dollar title from India and also the first billion-dollar IP for cricket," he said."You look at other sports and you look at what those sports have done broadly from a gaming IP perspective, they make billions of dollars in revenue, they touch hearts of millions and millions of fans worldwide. It also builds an economy for the ecosystem. You could have gaming influencers emerge from this tomorrow that would make millions of dollars on the back of being the best gamer. So it creates thousands of jobs and a lot of potential and opportunity for a lot of people."Shroff said LightFury has repeatedly encountered scepticism when it has spoken about building a AAA cricket game in India. The response, he said, has often been that the country already has several cricket games and none has managed to become a global franchise."When we would go and tell people we're building AAA titles, and cricket, they'd be like, AAA, really? India, and cricket, there are a dozen cricket games. How does it make you different? Same questions and the same thing, it can never become a global franchise. We've always believed it will. We truly know it will. And it's just about a lot of hard work and discipline and process that goes into building a AAA title," he said."The way India recognises and understands cricket, nobody in the world does. And we know the sport, we live it, breathe it, we watch every single game. Even if other countries are playing, we are sitting and watching it. That's how much we love the game. My point being, we know the game, we just need to know how to build it. And once we get it right, then it's a multi-billion-dollar opportunity."He does not dismiss the scepticism."These people are not wrong because we haven't done it right. So I think once we do is when things change. So if you ask me, can eCricket be that IP, I'd say 101%, but only time will tell if my words are true or not," he said."But we have all the ingredients and we're not building for something small. I can tell you one thing confidently. If we fail, we'll fail big, but we won't aim small. We won't build something that is mediocre."The company is yet to establish whether eCricket can hold an audience at the scale Shroff envisages. The early sign-ups, the licensed roster and the backing of prominent cricketers have given it a start, but the game will have to find players well beyond its initial audience."We have big dreams but we know till we make it, we've not made it. So we're going to work that hard to make sure that exactly what you said, cricket should have a global franchise. That's been the dream from day one and that's what we want to achieve with eCricket."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: GTA 6 PC scam alert: $200 malware kit targets gamers with fake downloads and crypto theft
articles.summary: GTA 6 fans waiting for a PC release have become targets of a dangerous online scam.
articles.body: GTA 6 fans waiting for a PC release have become targets of a dangerous online scam. Cybersecurity researchers have uncovered a $200 malware package that uses fake game downloads to trick players into infecting their computers. The toolkit reportedly combines account-stealing software, cryptocurrency theft tools and hidden mining programmes. With Rockstar Games yet to announce a native PC version, the promise of an unofficial download could cost players far more than they expect. The threat also reaches beyond gaming, potentially putting personal email, financial accounts and workplace information at risk.GTA 6 PC scam kit uses fake downloads to steal sensitive dataNordVPN’s Threat Intelligence team discovered the toolkit on November 16, three days before GTA 6 launched on consoles. According to the findings, the package was advertised on the dark web for $200, with buyers able to pay using Bitcoin or Tether.The toolkit reportedly includes several malicious programmes. One executable, named GTA6 Keygen.exe, is designed to capture browser session cookies. These files help websites keep users signed in. If criminals steal them, they may be able to access accounts without entering passwords or completing another two-factor authentication check.The package also contains a cryptocurrency wallet drainer targeting networks such as Ethereum, Solana, Polygon and BNB Smart Chain. Another component uses XMRig software to mine cryptocurrency secretly by consuming the victim’s computer resources.It even includes an automated YouTube Shorts tool that can promote fraudulent download links. This could help scammers reach more gamers through videos that appear connected to GTA 6.Rockstar has released the game for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, but has not announced a native PC version. Official cloud streaming on supported Xbox devices does not provide an installable PC copy.How to spot a fake GTA 6 download and protect your computerA website claiming to offer a free GTA 6 PC installer should raise immediate suspicion. Other warning signs include unofficial game ports, key generators, cracked files and links shared through unfamiliar social media accounts. Players should also avoid downloads that ask them to disable antivirus protection or connect a crypto wallet to unlock access.If you have downloaded a suspicious file but have not opened it, delete it and run a security scan. If you have already executed it, disconnect the computer from the internet and scan it with updated security software.Use a separate, trusted device to change important passwords, especially for email and banking accounts. Also sign out of active sessions, revoke unfamiliar devices and check financial and crypto accounts for unusual activity. If the computer connects to workplace systems, inform the organisation’s IT team.The discovery follows an earlier campaign involving fake GTA 6 demo websites that distributed Vidar malware. The latest findings suggest scammers are now packaging several harmful tools into one product. Until Rockstar announces an official PC release, players should treat any downloadable GTA 6 installer as a potential threat.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Rockstar's GTA 6 shatters entertainment launch records with a first-day haul that dwarfs GTA 5
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI made $3.79 billion in retail sales on its first day, Rockstar Games said Friday, the biggest entertainment launch ever recorded.
articles.body: Grand Theft Auto VI made $3.79 billion in retail sales on its first day, Rockstar Games said Friday, the biggest entertainment launch ever recorded. The figure covers worldwide sales through the end of Nov. 19, the day the game went on sale, and comes from company estimates. Rockstar also said 32.5 million copies sold before release. GTA V, the old record holder, made $815.7 million in its first 24 hours back in 2013. GTA VI cleared that mark more than four times over. Exactly how much came from pre-orders and how much from launch day is not clear yet.How big is GTA 6's launch compared with past entertainment records?Rockstar called the total a record for entertainment across any medium, and the comparisons back it up. Spider-Man: Brand New Day, this year's top-grossing film so far, made $2.5 billion across its entire run in cinemas. GTA 6 passed that in one day.Outside estimates had not come close. Trackers put GTA 6 at 19.1 million copies and about $1.84 billion by launch morning, well below what Rockstar reported. GTA V's 24-hour mark of 11.21 million copies had stood since 2013.Rockstar president and founder Sam Houser said, “We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world.” The standard edition costs $79.99 and the Ultimate Edition is $99.99. About three quarters of sales are on PlayStation 5, with the rest on Xbox. The series has now sold nearly 480 million units, and GTA V alone is near 235 million.Early reviews, server traffic and the cast behind Vice CityThe critics have been kind. GTA 6 holds a 99 Metascore, tying Ocarina of Time for the best mark on Metacritic. IGN called it an “uncompromisingly engineered” masterpiece. Players are less sure, with a user score of 5.0 out of 10 from nearly 4,000 ratings on Friday afternoon.The rush showed up online too. Traffic data had PS5 downloads in the UK peaking at 8.6 times normal levels around launch, and Rockstar's online services hit 11.2 times normal in Australia. New Zealand, where the game arrived first, jumped 14.8-fold four hours earlier, which suggests some players switched regions for early access. The 212GB file also broke Virgin Media O2's evening traffic record.Japan has censored parts of the game for its graphic content, and like earlier entries it is not approved for sale in mainland China. Police departments in the US also reminded players that street racing, auto theft and gun violence are still crimes.Rockstar has also named the cast. Manni L. Perez plays Lucia, Dylan Rourke plays Jason, and NFL star Tyreek Hill voices wide receiver Maleek Rivers. No date is set yet for a PC release or the multiplayer expansion.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Galán también se pierde el Major de México
articles.standfirst: El español continúa su recuperación de la lesión en la mano derecha que arrastra desde hace más de un mes y según ha sabido MARCA tiene la "ilusión" de estar en el Finals.
articles.summary: El español continúa su recuperación de la lesión en la mano derecha que arrastra desde hace más de un mes y según ha sabido MARCA tiene la "ilusión" de estar en el Finals.
articles.body: Ale Galán tampoco estará en el cierre de la temporada regular de Premier Padel y se perderá el Major de México que se celebra a partir del lunes en Acapulco. Una noticia que no por esperada deja de ser impactante porque, con este último torneo del año, el madrileño se habrá perdido un total de cuatro fechas consecutivas desde que pudiera jugar por última vez en Milán el pasado 17 de octubre. Tal y como confesó en MARCA el propio Galán "hemos optado por un tratamiento conservador para que vaya recuperando y el paso de las semanas, las pruebas y las resonancias dirán cómo avanza", explicaba sobre un plan revelador y que busca evitar el quirófano. Según ha podido conocer este periódico en los últimos días el español tiene la "ilusión" de estar en el Finals de Barcelona, el torneo donde juegan los 16 mejores del año, pero desde su entorno son precavidos con los plazos de recuperación. "Sigo esforzándome cada día con el objetivo del Finals", ha sido el mensaje con el que el propio jugador cerraba su mensaje en el que anunciaba la baja en Acapulco a través de sus redes sociales en la mañana de este sábado. Con apenas 20 días más por delante para el torneo de Barcelona y que se celebra del 10 al 13 de diciembre, Galán apura plazos en su recuperación y de momento no hay confirmación alguna, oficial o no, de si podrá estar en el último torneo del 2026.

articles.title: Spitting Image co-creator Peter Fluck dies aged 85
articles.summary: The 85-year-old he died in the early hours of Saturday at home in Cornwall, following a recent illness.
articles.body:
Peter Fluck, co-creator of award-winning satirical puppet show Spitting Image, has died aged 85.

His family said he died in the early hours of Saturday at home in Cornwall, following a recent illness.

Spitting Image was immensely popular and sometimes controversial, running from 1984-1996 across 18 seasons, and featured puppet caricatures of celebrities, politicians and royals, including former Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher and Queen Elizabeth the Queen Mother.

"The spirit that Spitting Image brought to the country was epoch defining," a family statement said.

"With Roger Law ('Luck and Flaw'), he brought a unique cutting edge to caricaturing that later evolved into a production company that created the TV series Spitting Image," it added.

"Peter's creative life continued after the series for many years from his studio in Cornwall. He was a private man who eschewed fame and attention."

The show won several awards, including one Bafta TV award and two Emmys and at its peak drew an audience of 15 million.

Fluck was born in Cambridge in 1941, and created the show alongside childhood friend Roger Law, who he met while studying at Cambridge School of Art.

Following school, both Fluck and Law moved to London and set up as freelance illustrators, and in 1976 set up their partnership 'Luck and Flaw' back in Cambridge.

"You could say we took the traditional newspaper editorial cartoon and put it on the screen," Fluck told ArtCornwall in an interview in 2006.

He described the show as being shown "at the difficult time of 10 o'clock on a Sunday night when all politicians should have been in bed".

Many of the characters included parodies of Thatcher's cabinet, with Douglas Hurd depicted with "Mr Whippy ice cream" hair, and her successor John Major caricatured as a dull, grey puppet with a penchant for peas.

"We did get quite a lot of approaches from politicians for their puppet to be made, because if you didn't appear as a puppet on Spitting Image you hadn't made it as a politician," Fluck said in an interview in 2011.

It was eventually axed by ITV because of declining audience numbers.

When he stepped away from the show, Fluck moved to Cornwall and focused his art on ceramics, printmaking and mobiles.

In 2018, Law donated his entire archive of Spitting Images to Cambridge University.

The collection - including original scripts, puppet moulds, drawings and recordings - was conserved and held in the library.

articles.title: Iran says held talks with Qatari mediators, urges US to accept conditions
articles.summary: Iran’s foreign minister says reopening the strait is ‘not difficult’ if the US accepts reasonable conditions.
articles.body:
Iran says Qatari mediators have travelled to Tehran as the country’s foreign minister urges the United States to accept Iranian conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

News of the talks came as the commander of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) toured an underground missile facility on Saturday and the country’s president said Iran is facing a “silent economic war”.

A Qatari delegation visited Tehran on Friday night and held two hours of talks with Iranian officials, Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said, according to Iran’s semi-official Tasnim news agency.

“We are in contact with mediators, including the Qataris, both in person and virtually, and are holding the necessary discussions to see whether another opportunity can be given to diplomacy,” he said on Saturday.

The US and Israel attacked Iran on February 28, prompting Tehran to launch strikes against Israel and Gulf states hosting US military bases. ⁠The conflict has drawn in countries across the region, disrupted shipping and ⁠pushed up global energy prices.

Gharibabadi said the talks have not yet become formal negotiations. If they do, the technical details of Iran’s nuclear programme would be discussed, he added, but Iran’s position is that its enriched uranium must not leave the country.

He also said Iran regards the US economic blockade as an act of war and will “take any action necessary” to break it.

For his part, US President Donald Trump told Fox News on Saturday that he wants a “permanent” deal that stops Iran from getting a nuclear weapon. He said Iranian officials are “very, very difficult”.

“We make a deal, and then they break the deal the next day,” he added.

The ongoing talks in the region “must be given a chance, and the blockade must be lifted rationally,” Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Saturday, according to state television.

“Our position is clear: as long as Iran’s demands are not met, the discussion on the Strait of Hormuz and its opening is pointless,” he said.

“At the same time, we have always affirmed our readiness for dialogue, just as we are ready to defend ourselves.”

Iran’s conditions have included ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending the US counter-blockade of Iranian ports.

Araghchi also said reopening the strait is “not difficult”, and requires the US only to “accept reasonable conditions that are in accordance with international law”, Tasnim reported.

The minister said there is “no solution” unless Washington acknowledges its mistakes and fulfils its previous commitments.

Iran has restricted shipping through the strait, which normally carried about a fifth of the world’s oil, since the war began. The US has imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports in response.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said on Saturday that his country is facing a “silent economic war” that is “tougher than a war with missiles”, according to the state news agency IRNA.

Pezeshkian told a meeting of investors and producers that “a group of bullies, oppressors, and coercers sought to bring down our country”, but that Iranian businesses had managed market conditions well.

He said the government was working to avoid power cuts over the winter.

Meanwhile, IRGC commander Major-General Ahmad Vahidi toured an underground missile facility, accompanied by Brigadier General Majid Mousavi, who heads the IRGC Aerospace Force, Tasnim reported.

Vahidi was briefed on the force’s readiness and recent developments in its missile programme.

The visit follows the Aerospace Force’s unveiling of a new underground facility earlier this month, where it displayed ballistic and cruise missiles and their launchers, Tasnim said.

The official method for robbing them doesn't come up until fairly late in the story, but there's a way to do it much sooner using a towing setup.If you are looking for further details about how you can rob ATMs in GTA 6, you can take a look at the section below.What you need to rob ATMsYou need a personal vehicle with a flatbed on the back. Not every vehicle will work, and the exact list of compatible vehicles hasn't been confirmed. Most basic trucks should be fine, so a standard pickup is the safest place to start. Make sure it's a vehicle you own, since you'll be modifying it.Listed below are the steps that you can then followStep 1: Visit a Mod ShopTake your truck to any Mod Shop. Because the winch is a basic modification, any shop will do, so you don't need to hunt down a specific one.Step 2: Install the winchWith your vehicle in the shop, follow these steps:Open the Bodywork section.Go to Towing.Select The Winch.That adds a towing hook to the back of your truck.Step 3: Hook the ATMFind an ATM and reverse your truck into it so the hook attaches. Line up the back of the vehicle carefully, since you need to make contact with the machine.Step 4: Rip it from the wallOnce the ATM is hooked, accelerate to pull it out of the wall. articles.title: Iran unveils dual-missile launcher, new ‘missile city’: What to know
articles.summary: Military officials tour underground facility in show of military capabilities despite US attacks.
articles.body:
Iran is putting its upgraded missile systems and underground military facilities on display, delivering a defiant message that it still has significant military capabilities despite US-Israeli attacks .

The latest showcase included a dual-missile launcher capable of firing two liquid-fuelled missiles simultaneously, according to state media broadcasting footage of military commanders touring an underground missile facility.

Officials insisted Iran has strengthened its missile and air-defence capabilities since previous rounds of fighting, including the launch of the US-Israel war in late February. Still, Iran is under mounting economic pressure from a naval blockade imposed by the United States that has disrupted its oil exports.

Here’s everything to know about the new dual-missile launcher and Iran’s “missile city”:

Iran has developed a range of ballistic and cruise missiles over the past three decades.

The new dual-missile launcher was unveiled as Major-General Ahmad Vahidi, commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), toured the underground facility on Saturday.

The IRGC aerospace force flaunted its range of upgraded missiles and military equipment, including the launcher, which is designed to carry and fire two liquid-fuelled missiles simultaneously, according to state broadcaster IRIB.

Liquid-fuelled missiles are launched vertically and offer speed-control capabilities, which can aid in overcoming air defence systems, IRIB reported.

State media said the latest generations of Iranian missiles have improved in range, accuracy and guidance capabilities independent of the US Global Positioning System (GPS).

What is known about the underground ‘missile city’?

Vahidi’s tour followed the IRGC aerospace force’s announcement of a new underground facility on November 10, according to the semiofficial Tasnim News Agency.

Tasnim said Iran is constructing underground military complexes able to continue weapons production and storage even under heavy bombardment.

The IRGC has said it transferred its missile and drone production lines from the surface to underground facilities to allow it continuing missile production.

Footage broadcast by IRIB on Saturday showed kilometres of tunnels and hundreds of missiles and launchers, including double launchers, among other systems.

Reporting from Tehran, Al Jazeera’s Resul Serdar said it was not clear when the state broadcaster’s footage of the underground site was filmed.

“The IRGC are trying to send a message to the outside world that they are not short of ammunition; they have enough missiles and enough launchers,” he said.

“If the war resumes again, they are going to deploy these capabilities,” he added. “It is a part of their propaganda, but also, Iran is flexing its muscles and trying to restore deterrence.”

Rami Khouri, a public policy fellow at the American University of Beirut, said Iran can safely store spare parts, raw materials and chemicals needed for creating missiles and drones at its underground sites in addition to storing finished missiles and drones.

Iran has been planning for such a scenario for decades, he said. “So there’s no doubt that Iran has stored an enormous amount of all of this,” Khouri, who is also a nonresident senior fellow at the Arab Center Washington DC, told Al Jazeera.

“They’ve shown … they’re prepared to stand sanctions and keep fighting.”

What is Iran trying to achieve by showcasing its defence capabilities?

Rob Geist Pinfold, a lecturer in international security at King’s College London, said Iran is now more emboldened than ever to assert its military capabilities due to the outcome of the US midterm elections, in which President Donald Trump’s Republican Party suffered sweeping losses.

The rising cost of living as a result of the war on Iran was a major factor in how people in the US voted in the elections, which saw Democrats winning control of both chambers of Congress.

“So [Trump] looks more like the boy who cried wolf,” Pinfold told Al Jazeera. “There seems to be a feeling that the US has been deterred or disincentivised from escalating the conflict.”

Khouri said Iran has taken a gradual approach to showing its technical and military capabilities as well as its political will to strike back.

“[This is] all designed to show the US and Israel … [that] Iran has very sophisticated capabilities that can both evade the Western defence forces and defence systems … and at the same time reach targets that it wants to hit in the countries that it decides to attack,” he said.

At the same time, Iran is suffering under the US naval blockade of its southern ports, so it feels the need to escalate because it feels backed into a corner, Pinfold noted.

He added that Iran’s economy is already in recession and there are growing fears it could suffer an even bigger hit.

“Very little if any oil is coming out of Iran at the moment,” Pinfold said.
