articles.title: Villavicencio car bomb: More than 20 injured in attack in Colombian city
articles.summary: The explosion is the latest in a string of attacks on buildings housing the security forces and government offices.
articles.body:
A car bomb has exploded in the central Colombian city of Villavicencio, injuring at least 23 people.

The explosive device was detonated in front of the offices of the regional government, in the city centre, damaging several buildings.

No group has so far admitted carrying out the attack - the latest in a series using explosives to target official buildings and security forces' headquarters.

Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella blamed "narcoterrorism", but gave no details. Armed criminal groups have recently stepped up attacks in what appears to be retaliation for an offensive ordered against them by De la Espriella.

Writing on social media, the president said that his government would "bluntly and forcefully" respond to "every drop of Colombian blood spilled".

"There will be no impunity and no retreat," he added.

And earlier on Monday, drones dropped explosives on the police headquarters in the northern city of Cúcuta.

The car bomb in Villavicencio went off on Monday evening - the eve of the 10th anniversary of the signing of a peace deal between the government and left-wing rebels of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (Farc), Colombia's largest guerrilla group.

Following the signing of the deal, thousands of left-wing rebel fighters laid down their arms.

However, a significant number of Farc members, who did not agree with the deal, refused to disarm and joined dissident groups instead.

While forced displacement, child recruitment and the numbers of attacks on security forces dropped in the aftermath of the deal, there has been an upsurge in recent years driven by dissident Farc factions and criminal groups fighting for control of drug trafficking, illegal mining and extortion rackets.

Colombia's first left-wing president, who was in power from August 2022 to August 2026, tried to negotiate with these armed groups as part of what he called his "total peace" strategy.

However, the talks stalled and collapsed with several of the criminal groups violating ceasefires they had agreed to observe.

De la Espriella was elected on a promise to crack down on "narcoterrorism" and has been scathing about his predecessor's approach.

He has also been critical of the 2016 agreement, calling it a "false peace".

In a post on X, uploaded shortly before news of the car bomb in Villavicencio spread, he referred to the peace deal as a "mess", describing it as a "waste of public resources" and the "cause behind Colombia's ruin".

Former President Juan Manuel Santos and Rodrigo Londoño - the two men who signed the peace deal on behalf of the Colombian government and the Farc respectively - defended it in an interview with BBC Mundo ahead of the anniversary .

Santos said that De la Espriella was "totally wrong" to call it a "false peace".

"He wants to use, or has bought into that cynical and mistaken theory that the violence we see today is the result of the peace deal, when the exact opposite is the case," Santos said, arguing that the problem lies with the lack of implementation of the agreement.

articles.title: Kelsey Hunter: Body found in search for missing 20-year-old woman
articles.summary: The body was recovered from a wooded area in Springholm in Dumfries and Galloway earlier this evening.
articles.body:
A body has been found in the search for a missing 20-year-old woman in Dumfries and Galloway.

Formal identification has not yet taken place but the family of Kelsey Hunter has been informed. She was last seen in Castle Douglas at 17:00 on Saturday and a major search has been taking place in her nearby home village of Springholm.

Daniel McKnight, 21, appeared on Tuesday on petition in Dumfries Sheriff Court charged with murder and two other charges, including defeating the ends of justice.

He made no plea and was remanded in custody.

Police say the body was recovered at about 19:15 from a wooded area in Springholm.

A post mortem examination will take place.

Det Ch Insp Stephen McGrath, of Police Scotland's Major Investigation Team, said officers are supporting her "heartbroken" family as extensive inquiries continue.

He said: "A team of officers are continuing to work around the clock to get them answers.

"This is clearly a significant development and extensive work remains ongoing.

"We are building up a picture of Kelsey's movements in the days and weeks prior to her being reported missing, and I would like to thank everyone for their help so far."

He asked any of her friends who have not yet spoke to officers to contact police .

A large police presence has been in the village - which sits next to the A75 road across the region - since Sunday evening.

The last sighting of Kelsey was on Cotton Street in Castle Douglas on Saturday.

Dogs, a helicopter and specialist officers were involved in the search while officers made door-to-door inquiries.

On Tuesday, a yellow police tent was seen in the entrance to a field yards from her home and officers in white forensic suits were spotted in the area.

Police said they had a dedicated team of officers working round the clock on the search.

Dumfries and Galloway Council said it had been offering support to the village primary, which sits close to where a cordon has been in place and at Castle Douglas High School where pupils would have known Kelsey.

"A message was shared with the Springholm school community earlier this afternoon, reassuring the community that the school continues to be a safe and nurturing space for our children," it said in a statement.

"The council's principal education psychologist has been on site at Springholm Primary School to provide support and will continue to visit and liaise with the school community of Springholm as well as the school community of Castle Douglas High School to provide support to learners and staff."

articles.summary: O temporal em Barra Mansa causou deslizamentos, interditou um imóvel e afetou o fornecimento de água após o transbordamento dos rios Barra Mansa e Bananal.
articles.body:

O temporal que atingiu Barra Mansa (RJ) entre a noite de quarta-feira (25) e a madrugada desta quinta-feira (26) provocou o transbordamento dos rios, deslizamentos de terra e interditou um imóvel. Segundo a prefeitura, os pluviômetros registraram, aproximadamente, 70 milímetros de chuva.

Ainda de acordo com o órgão, a cheia do Rio Barra Mansa atingiu principalmente os bairros Nova Esperança e Boa Sorte. As sirenes de alerta foram acionadas e dois pontos de apoio foram disponibilizados para receber moradores.

Ao todo, 12 pessoas precisaram ir para os abrigos. Segundo a prefeitura, após o nível da água baixar, todos os moradores já estavam retornando para as residências.

A administração pública informou que o transbordamento do Rio Bananal foi influenciado pela chuva em Resende (RJ), onde foram registrados 87 milímetros de precipitação. O aumento do nível do Rio Paraíba do Sul represou as águas do Bananal e também contribuiu para a cheia.

A Prefeitura informou ainda que foram registrados deslizamentos de terra na Rua Major José Bento, perto da Ponte Nilo Peçanha, no bairro Vila Coringa, onde um imóvel precisou ser interditado. Outro deslizamento foi identificado no bairro Jardim Central.

Ainda segundo a prefeitura, também foram registrados pontos de alagamento nas regiões da Colônia Santo Antônio e de Santa Maria II, associados à cheia do Rio Bananal.

Equipes da Defesa Civil e da Secretaria Municipal de Assistência Social e Direitos Humanos atuam desde a madrugada no atendimento às ocorrências. Os trabalhos continuam na manhã desta quinta-feira (26) e contam com o reforço do Serviço Autônomo de Água e Esgoto.

O órgão informou que os trabalhos concentram esforços na limpeza das áreas afetadas, no suporte às famílias atingidas e na vigilância dos níveis dos rios. Além disso, a distribuição de água pela Estação de Tratamento de Água (ETA) Colônia foi temporariamente interrompida devido à elevada turbidez da água, provocada pelas condições do Rio Bananal após as chuvas.

Para receber os alertas da Defesa Civil por SMS, os moradores da região devem se cadastrar enviando um SMS para o número 40.199, apenas com o número do CEP de onde mora, podendo digitar com ou sem hífen, com ou sem ponto.

articles.body: Indian esports organisations have expanded their competitive footprint internationally in recent years, fielding teams and players across a range of mobile, PC and console titles. Much of that expansion, particularly beyond mobile gaming, has involved recruiting talent from overseas, while the development of a similarly diverse pool of competitive talent within India remains a work in progress.The inaugural Esports Nations Cup (ENC) was supposed to be taking place this month. Instead, the focus has shifted to a year-long build-up to November 2027, with more opportunities for countries to experiment with team combinations, identify emerging talent and establish a competitive presence across a wider range of titles.For Nimish Raut, Global Head, Esports: Partnerships & Special Projects at NODWIN Gaming, India's National Team Partner for the ENC, the immediate priority remains building on the country's strengths in mobile gaming and challenging for championships and podium finishes, while gradually developing competitive capabilities across other platforms."You know, as somebody who's played multiple games and on multiple different platforms, I would definitely like it to be a mix of PC, console and mobile. See, you know, we have to do this step by step, right? The most obvious thing for us is to focus on our strength, which is obviously mobile gaming, and look at titles where we can definitely not just compete, but could actually be a very strong contender to either win the championship or be in the top three. So, 100 per cent focus on that by default, because of the strength that we bring to the table," Raut said in response to a TimesofIndia.com query during a media interaction outlining the Road to Esports Nations Cup 2027."Then there are certain areas where we do have the talent, we do have the skill. What we need to figure out, of course, is the right coaching and the right mindset. So definitely looking at shooter-specific titles from a PC perspective, I think that's where we will have huge scope to play around with."Brian Kraemer, Director of Product at the Esports Nations Cup, identified India as one of the biggest opportunities for the competition, both commercially and competitively."And then, competitively, I think there are obviously a lot of game titles where India is among the top contenders, whether it's chess, BGMI or other game titles. So I think it will be super interesting to see how the competitive side turns out. But from a potential perspective, I think India is huge and one of the biggest opportunities we have for ENC," Kraemer said.Indian clubs and their international rostersAt the Esports World Cup (EWC) in Paris earlier this year, three Indian teams - Team Apex Gaming, S8UL Esports and Total Gaming Esports - qualified for the Free Fire World Cup, marking India's maiden appearance in the competition. S8UL and Apex progressed to the Grand Finals, finishing 11th and 12th, respectively, while in the PUBG Mobile World Cup, GodLike Esports and Orangutan finished 13th and 15th, respectively.Four Indian grandmasters competed in chess, with Nihal Sarin and Arjun Erigaisi reaching the quarterfinals. In Trackmania, Kunal Upreti, popularly known as Spark, was India's lone representative, having finished second in the Asia and Oceania qualifiers.S8UL had announced rosters across 12 game titles ahead of the EWC, while GodLike, in its first year as an Esports Foundation Club Partner, recruited international talent across several disciplines, including Street Fighter 6, Tekken 8, Call of Duty: Warzone and Teamfight Tactics.In chess, while S8UL fielded three Indian grandmasters in Nihal, Aravindh Chithambaram and Pranesh M, Arjun represented South Korean organisation Gen.G and American grandmaster Hans Niemann competed for GodLike. Upreti's fellow Trackmania competitors at S8UL were Britain's Alexander Page and American Neal Kamdar.Even in titles where Indian clubs have established rosters comprising Indian players, national teams will have to be put together differently. One of the regulations introduced by the ENC prevents an entire club roster from being fielded as a national team."And that has two core reasons. One, we obviously want to make sure that fans get to see their dream teams and new line-ups, which they don't get to see frequently in their club ecosystems. But secondly, it would provide an inherent competitive advantage to any club roster that is consistently playing together and then becomes a national team competing against national teams that have to be formed from different clubs," Kraemer explained.The cost of competing beyond mobileAccording to the India State of Play 2026 report by Naavik and MIXI Global Investments, India has around 600 million gamers, with nearly eight billion mobile game downloads annually. Mobile gaming revenue, excluding real-money gaming, stood at an estimated USD 1.1 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 2.4 billion by 2029.The accessibility of smartphones and affordable internet has shaped much of the domestic esports market over the past decade, with mobile titles accounting for some of the country's biggest tournaments and drawing the investments of professional esports organisations.In an earlier interaction with TimesofIndia.com in May, S8UL founder and CEO Animesh Agarwal had spoken about the difficulties of scouting for PC players in India. In some titles, an organisation looking to put together a competitive roster might find only around 10 players of the required standard, while the cost of a gaming PC itself could run upwards of Rs 1.3-1.4 lakh.Agarwal had also pointed to the absence of a structured scouting programme for younger players, unlike traditional sports, where competitions at district, state and national levels provide opportunities for athletes to progress.When NODWIN was appointed India's National Team Partner in March, Raut had identified the unavailability of several game titles in India as one of the reasons the country had become somewhat disconnected from the global competitive ecosystem over the preceding years.India did not have a representative in the Asian Games 2026 version of PUBG Mobile, despite BGMI being among the country's most popular competitive gaming titles. The Esports Federation of India (ESFI) had dropped the game from its national selection process in March, citing regulatory considerations and the ban on PUBG Mobile in India.India has since secured representation across eight of the 16 titles at the ENC - Battlegrounds Mobile India (BGMI), Chess, EA Sports FC, Honor of Kings, MOBA Legends: 5v5!, Rocket League, Trackmania and VALORANT.While Nihal Sarin and EA Sports FC player Charanjot Singh earned direct invitations through the respective rankings, grandmaster Mitrabha Guha, Upreti and the Indian Rocket League and VALORANT teams secured their places through regional qualifiers.Those qualification slots will carry forward to 2027, with NODWIN also having the option of adding players to existing team rosters. In titles featuring five-player teams, for instance, national rosters can be expanded from seven to 10 players, with fresh opportunities to qualify in titles where India is yet to secure representation."Right now, with the roster expansion, it's up to the national teams to decide how they identify the players they want to add to the rosters. It can be tryouts, it can be national qualifiers, it can be other things. It's really up to the National Team Partners to decide," Kraemer said.The Esports Foundation has also earmarked USD 15 million for National Team Partners globally, covering expenses associated with team operations, player boot camps, staffing, marketing and regional events.Playing for India, and changing perceptions at homeNational representation in esports is not entirely new to Indian athletes. At the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya earlier this year, India fielded a 15-member contingent across four of the 11 esports medal events - League of Legends, Pokémon UNITE, eFootball and Puyo Puyo Champions - but returned without a medal.Paritosh went the furthest among the Indian competitors, reaching the quarterfinals of Puyo Puyo Champions before losing to eventual silver medallist Kang Dongshin of South Korea. India's League of Legends team, drawn from S8UL's roster, lost all three of its group-stage matches, while the eFootball and Pokémon UNITE campaigns also ended before the quarterfinals.When Agarwal spoke to TimesofIndia.com, he drew a comparison with Indian cricket and its 1983 World Cup triumph, a moment he believes Indian esports is still waiting for - an Indian player or team winning a global championship.It was a sentiment shared by NODWIN Gaming Senior Vice President Nishant Patel during an interaction in July, when he referred to co-founder Akshat Rathee's idea of a Neeraj Chopra moment for Indian esports.At the EWC in Paris in August, Mike McCabe, Chief Operating Officer of the Esports Foundation, had spoken to this website about his ambition of seeing professional esports players receive the kind of public recognition IPL cricketers enjoy in Indian cities. The inclusion of chess at the EWC, a game familiar to generations of Indian households, had also brought in audiences that would not necessarily follow competitive video gaming.For Raut, the prospect of Indian athletes competing as a national team also extends to a conversation that continues to take place in Indian households about the viability of gaming as a career."Yeah, I think for us, as a market, the fact that our athletes will represent the country, you know, there is a lot of chatter around whether esports or gaming is a good career. Is it something that should be pushed at a state level, at a school level, at a college level?"While India has continued to compete at the highest levels, given the social structure of the country, it's still a question mark sometimes in terms of how legitimate esports can be."And I think, both at a media level and at a consumer level, when people actually see these athletes travel to different parts of the world and now represent the country and potentially win medals and bring pride to the country, I think that is a great step for us as well," Raut said.Agarwal, on the other hand, had identified the availability of stable, long-term careers within gaming as an important factor in changing parental perceptions. Professional organisations now employ people in coaching, analytics, broadcast production and talent management, although the opportunities available to competitive players themselves remain uneven across game titles.Kraemer also sees greater scope for government involvement in esports through national teams, particularly at the grassroots level."I think especially the governmental support and recognition aspect is also one of the core things we want to achieve with the Esports Nations Cup."That may be a lot harder with the Esports World Cup because I think national-team activations and grassroots initiatives, etc., are much easier for governments to support and co-fund than specific club activations might be," he said.Raut had seen the interest generated by Indian creators attending the EWC and the viewership around the PUBG Mobile and BGMI broadcasts this year. Bringing some of the country's most popular players together in a national team is something he is particularly looking forward to."And I can only imagine what that fandom would be like when some of these popular players come together as a national team," Raut said.For now, though, there are players in other disciplines who may require more time and support before they are ready to compete internationally."And then, you know, there would be individual talents where I'm sure some kind of coaching, maybe international exposure, the right analytics, you know, having the right mindset, would help."Eventually, I would say, after maybe two or three seasons of the Nations Cup, I really hope that, as a country, we would be a multi-title and multi-platform country and not just a mobile-first market," Raut said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Major award for university's transformation of Edinburgh hospital
articles.summary: The Old Royal Infirmary was redeveloped as Edinburgh Futures Institute in an "extraordinary transformation".
articles.body:
The restoration of a Victorian hospital by a university in an "extraordinary transformation" has been awarded Scotland's biggest architecture prize.

The University of Edinburgh transformed the city's Old Royal Infirmary into a "radically collaborative space for learning and research" that has few, if any, parallels in recent UK architecture.

The NHS vacated the Category A-listed building in 2003 and it was purchased by the university in 2015 to become the Edinburgh Futures Institute.

Architects Bennetts Associates are credited with saving the Scottish Baronial structure from dereliction and have now secured the prestigious Andrew Doolan Best Building in Scotland Award.

Run by The Royal Incorporation of Architects in Scotland (RIAS), it is the country's foremost architecture accolade.

The prize was established in 2002 by Scots architect Doolan, and renamed in his honour after his death two years later.

Restored historic buildings make Scottish architecture shortlist

Home of the Year winner says renovating house was 'like childbirth'

Historic gardens project lands top architecture award

An outdoor swimming pool pavilion in Macduff, Aberdeenshire, and Paisley's central library in Renfrewshire also made this year's shortlist.

The Edinburgh restoration has been described as creating a landmark that "reveals its past with wit and pride".

While the fabric of the building was carefully restored, new accommodation and pavilions have been interwoven alongside the original wards and giant 492ft (150m) long corridors.

Flexible teaching, co-working and project areas are spread across five floors and include specialist facilities, such as digital maker spaces and exhibition zones.

The original clock tower has been reopened, now framed by a public plaza, above a 450-seat event space.

The award judges described The Edinburgh Futures Institute as a model for how architecture could bridge past, present, and future.

They said the "innovative integration of heritage and contemporary design" and social ambition had few, if any, parallels among recently completed buildings of this scale and complexity in the UK.

Technical mastery was highlighted in areas including corner turret escapes and structural reinforcements, and judges praised the precision and creativity while preserving the integrity of the historic David Bryce-designed building.

Libby Heathcote, president of the Royal Incorporation of Architects in Scotland (Rias), said the judges had reached a unanimous decision, despite the "exceptional execution" of the other shortlisted projects .

"The Edinburgh Futures Institute stood out for its civic generosity, scale and ambition," she said.

"Balancing loyalty to David Bryce's diagram with creativity in introducing bold new interventions is a remarkable achievement, blending historic Scottish Baronial architecture with modern innovation.

"The result is a modern, welcoming, clever, and stimulating place that people want to work in and return to."

articles.title: Coki Nieto se queda fuera del Tour Finals de Barcelona
articles.standfirst: El madrileño no estará en el último torneo del curso donde se reúnen los 16 mejores jugadores del año tras caer en octavos del México Major
articles.summary: El madrileño no estará en el último torneo del curso donde se reúnen los 16 mejores jugadores del año tras caer en octavos del México Major
articles.body: Coki Nieto no estará en el Premier Finals de Barcelona de Premier Padel. La eliminación del madrileño junto a Mike Yanguas ante Íñigo Jofre y Juanlu Esbrí en octavos del México Major ha provocado que el revés que dio el quinto Mundial de Pádel a España -junto a Coello- se haya quedado fuera definitivamente del torneo en el que jugarán los 16 mejores de la temporada según el ranking. Las lesiones han lastrado la temporada de Coki, que no jugó ni en Riad ni en Düsseldorf ni en Milán en un 2026 en la que ha compartido pista con Jon Sanz, primero, y con Mike Yanguas, después. La derrota en Acapulco provoca que no esté en una de las citas más esperadas que se celebrará en el Palau Sant Jordi de Barcelona. Otros dos que se jugaban el Premier Padel Tour Finals son Javi Leal y Tino Libaak, que se enfrentarán junto a sus parejas Fran Guerrero y Gonzalo Alfonso este viernes en la jornada de cuartos de final del último grande de la temporada de Premier Padel 2026. Los españoles tumbaron a Goñi y Alonso, mientras que los argentinos dieron la sorpresa ante Stupaczuk y Sanz. Un triunfo de la dupla albiceleste metería directamente al drive de San Luis en el último torneo de la temporada y de esta manera complicaría mucho también la presencia de Maxi Arce y de Juan Tello, que ya cayeron en dieciseisavos ante Valenzuela y Gil.

articles.title: GTA 6 player who lost his wife of 50 years gets emotional after seeing Jason open the car door for Lucia
articles.summary: GTA 6 has given players many small details to enjoy, but one of them has touched a player in a very personal way.
articles.body: GTA 6 has given players many small details to enjoy, but one of them has touched a player in a very personal way. Joe Shaw, who lost his wife of 50 years four years ago, became emotional after seeing Jason Duval open the car door for Lucia Caminos in the game. While some players have made fun of GTA 6's relationship features, Shaw found a special meaning in this simple action. It reminded him of a loving habit he shared with his late wife.GTA 6's Jason opening the car door for Lucia reminds player of his late wifeA GTA 6 player shared his experience in a GTA 6 Facebook fan group. He explained that his wife, who passed away after suffering a stroke four years ago, always loved it when he opened the car door for her.She would call him a "real gentleman" whenever he did it. It was a small act, but it remained a special part of their 50-year marriage.While playing GTA 6, Shaw noticed that Jason could open the car door for Lucia. The action also gives the couple a small boost in their in-game relationship. However, for Shaw, it was much more than just another game feature.Seeing Jason perform the same action brought back memories of his wife and the time they spent together. Even Lucia's reactions reminded him of the little moments he once shared with her.For many players, opening a car door might seem like an ordinary action. But for Shaw, it brought back memories of someone he had loved for five decades.While GTA 6 players mock Jason and Lucia's relationship, one widower finds a special meaningGTA 6's relationship features have become a topic of debate among players. Some have made fun of the way Jason goes out of his way to keep Lucia happy. They have also mocked activities such as buying flowers, running errands and spending time together.Some players have even called the game a "cuck simulator" because of the way Jason behaves around Lucia.However, Shaw's experience shows that these small actions can mean something very different to different people. What some players see as unnecessary tasks, he sees as a reminder of the love he shared with his wife.Rockstar Games has incorporated all sorts of day-to-day activities and relationship interactions between Jason and Lucia. These details also contribute to the representation of the two characters’ life and behavior as a couple.Shaw’s story also illustrates how video games can sometimes trigger real-life memories in surprising ways. One act in a virtual world restored 50 years of love, care and companionship.GTA 6 players might still debate its relationship features, but Shaw has found a personal reason to love them.
